passage.title: Teacher-written extract for TGA
paras: The storm did not arrive; it invaded. It marched over the hills in grey columns, flattened the barley, and hammered at every shutter in the village. Inside the bakery, Amira pressed her palm against the trembling glass and watched the street surrender, one gutter at a time.

head: Word or phrase
Connotation
Effect
rows: the storm feels hostile and purposeful

model.title: How does the writer present the storm?

parts.text: Zoom in: 'surrender' suggests the village gives up
Analyse: nature is presented as a conqueror
Alternative: 'trembling glass' suggests fear inside as well as damage outside

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: The writer presents the storm as an invading army: the verb 'invaded' and the image of 'grey columns' build a military metaphor, so that when the street 'surrender[s]' the village seems conquered.

keywords.def: notes written on a text to explore meaning
the ideas and feelings a word suggests

questions.a: violent, repeated blows; the storm feels relentless

questions.q: Core: annotate a second unseen extract for five connotations, then write a PETZAAL paragraph

questions.a: A named semantic field with three words

questions.a: An explanation of pace and effect

questions.q: Which semantic field runs through the extract?
questions.a: A) war and invasion. invaded, marched, columns, surrender all belong to war.
